name: Vesper-Kyre

civilization.name: The Kyre Chorus
civilization.notes: A networked civilization that abandoned its bodies for orbital computation; the planet-wide silence followed within a single generation.

description: Vesper-Kyre is a world embalmed: forests of stone trees stand in wind-carved ranks across three continents, their petrified limbs still bearing the shapes of leaves, while rivers of dust flow through channels cut by water that vanished before human language existed. The sky is a thin violet haze over tan nothing, horizon to horizon.

The silence is not empty but held, like breath. Wind moving through the stone forest produces tones—precise, repeating, almost melodic—and travelers report the unsettling certainty that the pitch changes when they are observed. Dust devils cross the dead seas in straight lines.

The Kyre Chorus ruled this world and then the surrounding system, until they migrated wholesale into computational substrates left unexplained; the last biological record is a planetary census, and the first archaeological layer above it is undisturbed dust. Their cities remain intact and swept clean, arranged around black monoliths that predate every ruin and hum at two degrees above absolute zero. And from somewhere in orbit—no object has ever been found—a narrowband signal repeats on a schedule the monoliths' spacing matches exactly.

Exotic matter traces around the ruins would fund a dozen research empires, and salvage rights are contested in four courts. But the teams that camp overnight in the stone forests all file the same addendum to their reports: the wind-tones have begun including, unmistakably, fragments of each visitor's own voice.
